lines: This fire is real.
NASA lit it on purpose, inside an empty cargo spaceship, high above the Earth.
Because one day, people will live on the Moon... and up there, fire won't behave the way it does here.
We're a team of six at NASA Space Apps Bangladesh, and we built MicroFire Atlas on three promises.
Never fake a number. Every value is traced to the exact page of a NASA report.
Build for everyone: the planner choosing the air for a Moon base, and the kid who may live there one day.
And always show where the evidence stops.
In 1967, a fire in a pure-oxygen cabin killed the three astronauts of Apollo 1, during a test on the launch pad.
Fire is still a serious risk for every crew. And in space, it changes.
It affects every astronaut who will sleep in a Moon habitat, and every engineer who must decide what air they breathe.
Without gravity, nothing rises. A flame turns small, round and blue, and lives on the air drifting past it.
NASA is studying Moon habitat air with lower pressure and more oxygen. Decades of fire tests exist, scattered across reports.
So we gathered them. Seventy-eight test records. Sixty-two verified findings. And not one test at thirty-four percent oxygen.
MicroFire Atlas turns that scattered evidence into one mission tool.
One mission tool
Ask what NASA knows about fire in a lunar habitat. It finds the records, compares every condition, and ranks NASA's own findings, explaining every rank.
Find · compare · rank
The Mission Analyst runs any cabin atmosphere NASA has studied. Every tick under a slider is a real NASA test.
Every tick is a real NASA test
Then it shows exactly where the evidence stops. Ask for a fire probability, and its machine-learning model refuses: prediction blocked.
Even the ML says no
Change the ranking weights a thousand ways, and it shows which answers still hold.
1,000 variations per ranking
Its AI answers only from NASA evidence, and a checker catches made-up numbers and Moon claims drawn from orbit tests.
Every claim checked
And in the Flame Lab, anyone can run NASA's wind tunnel in 3D, and see the moment the evidence runs out.
Flame Lab · in 3D
What changes? Planners see the gap before a crew ever breathes that air.
See the gap first
Our planner shows which hypothetical experiment would answer the most open questions, and where NASA's planned Moon burns already fit.
Research planner
Planners get a printable evidence brief, researchers get open data, and children get a reason to love science.
Brief · open data · young explorers
Next, we need fire scientists to review our labels, and real flame frames annotated by people.
One day, every new NASA fire test could plug straight into this map.
MicroFire Atlas.
Real NASA data. A real adventure. And honest answers about what we still don't know.
Come follow the spark.
